label: rem:n2
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:n2}
For $n=2$, Theorem~\ref{thm:symmetric-Grassmann} reduces exactly to the classical Grassmann formula. Indeed, $c_{2,2}=1/2$, and the same intersection $V_1\cap V_2$ occurs once with distinguished index $1$ and once with distinguished index $2$.
head: environment

label: sum-n=3
title: Example
body_md:
For $n=3$, Theorem~\ref{thm:symmetric-Grassmann}
recovers the identity in \cite[Exercise~20, Section~2C]{Axler24}:
\begin{equation}\label{sum-n=3}
\dim(V_1+V_2+V_3)=\sum_{i=1}^{3}\dim(V_i)
-\frac{1}{3}\sum_{1\leq i<j\le3}\dim(V_i\cap V_j)-\frac{1}{3}\sum_{i=1}^{3}
\dim\Bigl(V_i\cap\!\sum_{j\in[3]\setminus\{i\}}V_j\Bigr).
\end{equation}
Here the coefficient $1/3=2\,c_{3,2}$ arises by collecting
the identical terms corresponding to $V_i\cap V_j$ and
$V_j\cap V_i$. More generally, collecting the pairwise
terms over $i<j$ gives the coefficient
$2\,c_{n,2}=1/\binom{n}{2}$.
The first correction records pairwise overlap, while the
second captures, in particular, the genuinely non-distributive
phenomenon that a subspace may meet the sum of two others
nontrivially even when all pairwise intersections vanish.

Theorem~\ref{thm:TMS-comparison} makes explicit that the two identities \eqref{sym-Grassmann} and \eqref{TMS-formula} resolve the same total dimension correction through different subspace data. The Tian--Makrides--Szemberg expression uses the maximal proper sums $W_i$ and their common intersection $Y$. \label{rem:expected}
In the predecessor notation, the allocation to $V_i$ takes
the form
\begin{equation}
\phi_i(\mathfrak{r})=\mathtt{E}\Bigl[\dim(V_i)-
\dim\Bigl(V_i\cap\sum_{j\in\operatorname{Pred}_{\pi}(i)}V_j\Bigr)\Bigr],
\end{equation}
where $\pi$ is uniformly distributed on $\mathfrak{S}_n$.
This allocated share need not be an integer.
For instance, in Example~\ref{ex:three-lines}, the first
two lines in any ordering each contribute one new dimension,
whereas the last contributes none. Each line therefore
receives a share of $2/3$ of the total dimension $2$.

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:n4}
For $n=4$, the coefficients in Theorem~\ref{thm:symmetric-Grassmann} are $\frac{1}{12}$ for $|S|=1$, $\frac{1}{12}$ for $|S|=2$, and $\frac{1}{4}$ for $|S|=3$. Thus, $\operatorname{def}(V_1,V_2,V_3,V_4)=A_2+A_3+A_4$, where $A_2\leq A_3\leq A_4$. The equality separates pairwise overlap, three-subspace overlap with a distinguished member, and one-versus-all-others overlap without introducing alternating inclusion--exclusion terms.

label: cor:Bk-quotient
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Quotient intersections and vanishing curvature

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Q_S:V\to V/U_S$ be the quotient map. Its restriction to $V_j\cap(V_l+U_S)$ has image $\overline{V}_j^{\,S}\cap\overline{V}_l^{\,S}$ and kernel $V_j\cap U_S$. Hence
\[
\dim(\overline{V}_j^{\,S}\cap\overline{V}_l^{\,S})
=\dim\bigl(V_j\cap(V_l+U_S)\bigr)-\dim(V_j\cap U_S).
\]
Substitute this identity into Proposition~\ref{prop:Bk-local}. Each unordered pair occurs twice in its ordered-pair sum, and
\[
n\binom{n-1}{k-1}(n-k)=2\binom{n}{k-1}\binom{n-k+1}{2}.
\]
This gives \eqref{Bk-quotient}. Since every summand is nonnegative, $B_k=0$ precisely when all quotient intersections vanish. Taking their inverse images under $Q_S$ gives \eqref{Bk-zero-quotient}.

label: thm:common-core
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Common-core rigidity

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~ef{thm:exact-gap}, equality in either endpoint bound holds if and only if $B_k=0$ for every $2\leq k\leq n-1$. Hence conditions (i), (ii), and (iii) are equivalent. Assume (iii). Using $M_{i,s}$ and its monotonicity from the proof of Theorem~ef{thm:Ak-monotone}, $A_n-A_2=0$ forces $M_{i,n-1}=M_{i,1}$ for every $i$. For fixed $i$ and every $j
eq i$, each $\dim(V_i\cap V_j)$ is at most $\dim(V_i\cap\sum_{k
e i}V_k)=M_{i,n-1}$, while their average is $M_{i,1}=M_{i,n-1}$. Hence every one of these dimensions equals $M_{i,n-1}$, and containment gives $V_i\cap V_j=V_i\cap\sum_{k
e i}V_k$ for all $j
e i$. Since $V_i\cap V_j=V_j\cap V_i$, these spaces have a common value for all $i$, and that value is $D= igcap_{i\in[n]}V_i$. This proves (iv). Condition (iv) is equivalent to $(V_i/D)\cap\sum_{j
eq i}(V_j/D)=\{0\}$ for every $i$, which is the standard direct-sum criterion for the quotient family. Thus (iv) and (v) are equivalent. Choosing complements $U_i\subseteq V_i$ such that $V_i=D\oplus U_i$ shows that (v) and (vi) are equivalent. Finally, assume (iv). For every nonempty $S\subseteq[n]\setminus\{i\}$, we have $D\subseteq V_i\cap\sum_{j\in S}V_j\subseteq V_i\cap\sum_{j
eq i}V_j=D$. Thus every intersection dimension defining $A_k$ equals $\dim(D)$, so $A_2=\cdots=A_n=\dim(D)$. This proves (iii), completes the equivalence, and establishes \eqref{kth-defect-Ak-common-core}. Equation~\eqref{def-common-core} follows from Corollary~ef{cor:defect-decomposition}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: For families of subspaces of equal dimension, condition~\textnormal{(iv)} is the defining property of a sunflower of maximal dimension in \cite[Section~2]{BSSV17}. For such families with constant pairwise intersection dimension, a characterization by successive rank increments is given in \cite[Remark~1.3]{LST22}. Theorem~\ref{thm:common-core} characterizes the common-core decomposition for arbitrary finite subspace families through equality in either averaged defect bound.

label: def:average-rank
title: Definition
head: environment
name: Average rank profile

label: thm:average-rank
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Average-rank representation

label: pointed-rank
title: Proof
body_md:
For $T\subseteq[n]$ with $|T|=k$ and $i\in T$,
the classical Grassmann formula gives
\begin{equation}\label{pointed-rank}
\dim\Bigl(V_i\cap\sum_{j\in T\setminus\{i\}}V_j\Bigr)=
\dim(V_i)+\dim\Bigl(\sum_{j\in T\setminus\{i\}}V_j\Bigr)
-\dim\Bigl(\sum_{j\in T}V_j\Bigr).
\end{equation}
Average \eqref{pointed-rank} over all pairs $(T,i)$ with $|T|=k$ and $i\in T$. The first term averages to $R_1$, the second to $R_{k-1}$, and the third to $R_k$. This proves \eqref{kth-defect-Ak-Rk}. Equation~\eqref{kth-defect-Ak-Delta} follows immediately. Taking the difference of \eqref{kth-defect-Ak-Rk} at levels $k+1$ and $k$ gives $B_k=A_{k+1}-A_k=2R_k-R_{k-1}-R_{k+1}=\Delta_k-\Delta_{k+1}$. Since $B_k\ge0$, one has $\Delta_2\geq\cdots\geq\Delta_n$. The remaining first step follows from $\Delta_1-\Delta_2=A_2\geq0$. This proves \eqref{Rk-concave}.

label: rem:rank-curvature
title: Remark
head: environment

label: ex:same-defect-different-profiles
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:same-defect-different-profiles}
Let $e_1,e_2,e_3$ be the standard basis of $\mathbbm{F}^3$ and consider the two arrangements
\begin{align*}
U&\coloneq\bigl(\operatorname{span}\{e_1\},
\operatorname{span}\{e_1+e_2\},
\operatorname{span}\{e_2\},
\operatorname{span}\{e_3\}\bigr), \\
W&\coloneq\bigl(\operatorname{span}\{e_1\},
\operatorname{span}\{e_2\},
\operatorname{span}\{e_3\},
\operatorname{span}\{e_1+e_2+e_3\}\bigr).
\end{align*}
Both have total dimension defect $1$. Their average-rank profiles are
\[
(R_0,R_1,R_2,R_3,R_4)(U)=\Bigl(0,1,2,\frac{11}{4},3\Bigr),
\qquad
(R_0,R_1,R_2,R_3,R_4)(W)=(0,1,2,3,3).
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:average-rank} therefore gives
\[
(A_2,A_3,A_4)(U)=\Bigl(0,\frac{1}{4},\frac{3}{4}\Bigr),
\qquad
(A_2,A_3,A_4)(W)=(0,0,1).
\]
The successive gaps $B_k=A_{k+1}-A_k$ are
\[
(B_2,B_3)(U)=\Bigl(\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{2}\Bigr),
\qquad
(B_2,B_3)(W)=(0,1).
\]
Thus $U$ has positive curvature at both levels, whereas the curvature of $W$ is concentrated at the final level. Figure~\ref{fig:rank-defect-profiles} compares the average-rank and dimension-defect profiles of these two arrangements. The defect profile distinguishes dependence visible at intermediate levels from dependence visible only at the final level, even when the individual dimensions and total defect agree.
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{Grassmann_defect_profiles.png}
\caption{Average-rank profiles (a) and dimension-defect profiles (b) of the arrangements $U$ and $W$ in Example~\ref{ex:same-defect-different-profiles}. Blue solid lines with circles represent $U$; orange dashed lines with squares represent $W$. Both arrangements have total dimension defect $1$, but their profiles distinguish dependence at intermediate levels from dependence appearing only at the final level.} \label{fig:rank-defect-profiles}
\end{figure}

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:defect-decomposition} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:Ak-monotone} to $V_1^\circ,\ldots,V_n^\circ$.
The annihilator identities \eqref{annihilator} identify their total defect
with $\operatorname{def}^\vee$ and their $k$-th graded defect with $A_k^\vee$, since
\begin{equation*}
\Bigl(V_i+\bigcap_{j\in T\setminus\{i\}}V_j\Bigr)^\circ
=V_i^\circ\cap\sum_{j\in T\setminus\{i\}}V_j^\circ.
\end{equation*}
Both assertions follow.

head: environment
name: Symmetrized Kinser slack

title: Proof
body_md: Under uniform permutation averaging, a rank term on $k$ distinct labels has average $R_k$. In \eqref{Kinser-slack}, the total coefficients of singleton, pair, and triple ranks are respectively $-(n-2)$, $3+2(n-3)-1=2(n-2)$, and $-(n-2)$. The average is therefore $(n-2)(2R_2-R_1-R_3)$, which equals $(n-2)B_2$ by \eqref{defect-gap-Bk-Rk}.

label: rem:Kinser-symmetry-collapse
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Kinser-symmetry-collapse}
Theorem~\ref{thm:symmetrized-Kinser} shows that complete permutation symmetry removes the additional directional information carried by an individual Kinser inequality: the fully averaged Kinser slack is exactly a multiple of the first curvature $B_2$ of the average rank profile. Thus the representability-specific information in the Kinser hierarchy is inherently nonsymmetric with respect to the labels, whereas its fully symmetric component is already encoded by the graded defect hierarchy.

label: thm:conditioned-Kinser
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Conditioned Kinser representation of the defect gaps

label: fixed-S-Kinser
title: Proof
head: environment

label: cor:Kinser-Br-zero
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Kinser-Br-zero}
For $2\leq k\leq n-2$, one has $B_k=0$ if and only if $\mathcal{K}_{n-k+2}^{S,\pi}=0$ for every $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|=k-2$ and every $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}([n]\setminus S)$. Equivalently, every ordered quotient arrangement obtained by contracting a set of $k-2$ subspaces attains equality in the corresponding Kinser inequality.
head: environment
name: Kinser rigidity for vanishing defect curvature

title: Proof
body_md: Every quotient arrangement in \eqref{defect-gap-Bk-Kinser-average} is again linearly representable. Hence each Kinser slack $\mathcal{K}_{n-k+2}^{S,\pi}$ is nonnegative by \eqref{Kinser-nonnegative}. Formula~\eqref{defect-gap-Bk-Kinser-average} therefore expresses $B_k$ as a positive constant times the average of nonnegative quantities. The average vanishes if and only if every summand vanishes.
head: environment

label: rem:Kinser-defect-bridge
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Kinser-defect-bridge}
Theorem~\ref{thm:conditioned-Kinser} provides a direct bridge between two different hierarchies. The quantities $B_k$ arise from the symmetric dimension-defect hierarchy and measure the discrete curvature of the average rank profile, while the Kinser inequalities encode additional constraints imposed by linear representability. For $2\leq k\leq n-2$, the curvature $B_k$ equals $1/(n-k)$ times the average Kinser slack of quotient arrangements obtained by contracting $k-2$ subspaces, where the average is taken over both the contraction sets and the orderings of the remaining subspaces. In particular, the full symmetrization of a representability-specific inequality does not produce a new symmetric inequality beyond the submodular curvature $B_k\geq0$; instead, the additional representability information is retained in the individual, nonsymmetrized Kinser slacks. The final curvature $B_{n-1}$ has no counterpart in this construction, since the Kinser hierarchy begins with four subspaces.
head: environment

label: ex:final-curvature
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:final-curvature}
                                             
Let $n\geq4$, let $e_1,\ldots,e_{n-1}$ be the standard basis of $\mathbbm{F}^{n-1}$, and set
\[
V_i=\operatorname{span}\{e_i\}\quad(1\leq i\leq n-1),
\qquad\qquad
V_n=\operatorname{span}\{e_1+\cdots+e_{n-1}\}.
\]
Every proper selection of these lines is independent, whereas the full selection has rank $n-1$. Thus
\[
R_k=\min\{k,n-1\},\qquad A_2=\cdots=A_{n-1}=0,\qquad A_n=1,
\]
and
\[
B_2=\cdots=B_{n-2}=0,\qquad B_{n-1}=1.
\]
By Corollary~\ref{cor:Kinser-Br-zero}, every contracted Kinser slack appearing in Theorem~\ref{thm:conditioned-Kinser} vanishes, although the total dimension defect is $1$. This arrangement exhibits explicitly the dependence measured by the final curvature and omitted from that contraction construction.

label: prop:entropy-correspondence
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $T\subseteq[n]$ and $i\in T$,
\[
I(X_i;X_{T\setminus\{i\}})=H(X_i)+H(X_{T\setminus\{i\}})-H(X_T).
\]
Averaging over all pairs $(T,i)$ with $|T|=k$ gives \eqref{Ak-mutual-information}, since the three terms have averages $\overline{H}_1$, $\overline{H}_{k-1}$, and $\overline{H}_k$, respectively. Taking successive differences in \eqref{entropy-defects} gives
\[
B_k^{H}=2\overline{H}_k-\overline{H}_{k-1}-\overline{H}_{k+1}.
\]
For distinct $i,j\notin S$,
\[
I(X_i;X_j\mid X_S)=H(X_{S\cup\{i\}})+H(X_{S\cup\{j\}})-H(X_S)-H(X_{S\cup\{i,j\}}).
\]
Average this identity over all triples $(S,i,j)$ with $|S|=k-1$ and distinct $i,j\notin S$. The four terms have averages $\overline{H}_k$, $\overline{H}_k$, $\overline{H}_{k-1}$, and $\overline{H}_{k+1}$, respectively. There are $n\binom{n-1}{k-1}(n-k)$ such triples. This gives \eqref{Bk-conditional-mutual-information}. Finally, summing $A_k^{H}=\overline{H}_1+\overline{H}_{k-1}-\overline{H}_k$ over $2\leq k\leq n$ gives \eqref{total-correlation}. Nonnegativity of mutual and conditional mutual information gives $A_k^H\geq0$ and $B_k^H\geq0$, respectively. For $2\leq k\leq n-1$, $2\overline{H}_k-\overline{H}_{k-1}-\overline{H}_{k+1}=B_k^H\geq0$, while the first step is $2\overline{H}_1-\overline{H}_0-\overline{H}_2=A_2^H\geq0$. Together these inequalities establish discrete concavity of the full average entropy profile.
head: environment
